elements.label: Figure 7.3
elements.description:
Chart type: two-panel stacked bar chart with a net-effect line overlay, by per capita market income decile (1-10). Legend series: SI, Subsidies, Direct taxes, Education, Education OOP, VAT, Excise, Health, Health OOP, Environmental, Direct transfer, Net effect.

Panel A: Absolute incidence (total tax collected and spending received). Y-axis: Monthly VND (thousands), ticks at 1000, 500, 0, -500, -1000, -1500, -2000, -2500, -3000. X-axis: Per capita market income decile 1-10. Positive stacked bars (spending received, roughly ~300-400 per decile) sit above zero; negative stacked bars (taxes paid) grow with income. Net effect line falls from ~+250 in decile 1 to ~-300 in decile 6, ~-600 in decile 8, ~-1000 in decile 9 and ~-2400 in decile 10. Decile 10 bars extend to roughly -2,700, dominated by SI (teal), VAT (grey), direct taxes and health contributions.

Panel B: Relative incidence (tax collected and spending received as a percentage of household market income). Y-axis: Percent of market income, ticks from -60 to 40 in steps of 10. Positive bars are largest in decile 1 (top ~45%, driven by direct transfers, education and health spending); the net effect line falls from ~+35% in decile 1 to ~+12% in decile 2, ~+6% in decile 3, ~+2% in decile 4, ~-3% in decile 5, ~-7% in decile 6, ~-10% in decile 7, ~-13% in decile 8, ~-17% in decile 9 and ~-22% in decile 10.

Pattern: the net effect is strongly positive for the poorest deciles and becomes increasingly negative toward the richest deciles in both panels.

Note: See Annex 7.1 for key assumptions. Source: 2018 VHLSS and World Bank calculations.

Bars are grouped by brackets: Direct transfer; Direct taxes (PIT, Other direct taxes, SSC/HI); Indirect subsidies (Electricity subsidy); Indirect taxes (VAT, Excise, Environmental tax).

Approximate readings (values not printed):
- Cash transfer: ~1.1 (positive, reduces poverty)
- PIT: ~0.05 (small positive, floating near 1.0)
- Other direct taxes: ~0.05 (small positive, floating near 0.95-1.0)
- SSC/HI: ~0.3 (floating from ~0.65 to ~0.92)
- After direct and indirect taxes and transfers (consumable income): ~0.65 (positive)
- Electricity subsidy: ~0.15 (floating from ~0.65 to ~0.8)
- VAT: ~0.8 (positive)
- Excise: ~-0.3 (negative, increases poverty)
- Environmental tax: ~-0.05 (small negative)
- After direct and indirect taxes: ~-0.35 (negative, net increase in poverty)

Pattern: transfers and direct taxes/subsidies reduce poverty, while excise, environmental and the overall after-tax result increase poverty, with VAT offsetting the others.

Note: Marginal effects on poverty reduction are presented. A positive bar represents contribution to poverty reduction; a negative bar represents an increase in poverty. Source: 2018 VHLSS and World Bank calculations.
